helpFullQuotes.build:
Build an Aiken project

Usage: aiken build [OPTIONS] [DIRECTORY]

Arguments:
  [DIRECTORY]
          Path to project

Options:
  -D, --deny
          Deny warnings; warnings will be treated as errors

  -S, --silent
          Silence warnings; warnings will not be printed

  -w, --watch
          When enabled, re-run the command on file changes instead of exiting

  -u, --uplc
          Also dump textual uplc

      --env <ENV>
          Environment to build against

  -o, --out <FILEPATH>
          Optional relative filepath to the generated Plutus blueprint.
          
          [default: plutus.json]

  -f, --trace-filter <TRACE_FILTER>
          Filter traces to be included in the generated program(s).
          
            - user-defined:
                only consider traces that you've explicitly defined
                either through the 'trace' keyword of via the trace-if-false
                ('?') operator.
          
            - compiler-generated:
                only included internal traces generated by the
                Aiken compiler, for example in usage of 'expect'.
          
            - all:
                include both user-defined and compiler-generated traces.
          
          [optional] [default: all]
          
          [possible values: user-defined, compiler-generated, all]

  -t, --trace-level <TRACE_LEVEL>
          Choose the verbosity level of traces:
          
            - silent:
                disable traces altogether
          
            - compact:
                only culprit line numbers are shown on failures
          
            - verbose:
                enable full verbose traces as provided by the user or the compiler
          
          [optional]
          
          [default: silent]
          [possible values: silent, compact, verbose]

  -I, --include-all-types
          Include all serialisable types in the blueprint, not only those present in validators
          signatures. Off by default

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
helpFullQuotes.apply:
Apply a parameter to a parameterized validator

Usage: aiken blueprint apply [OPTIONS] [CBOR]

Arguments:
  [CBOR]
          The parameter, as a Plutus Data (CBOR, hex-encoded).
          
          For example, `182A` designates an integer of value 42. If you're unsure about the shape of
          the parameter, look at the schema specified in the project's blueprint (i.e.
          `plutus.json`), or use the `cbor.serialise` function from the Aiken standard library.

Options:
  -i, --in <FILEPATH>
          Optional path to the blueprint file to be used as input.
          
          [default: plutus.json]

  -o, --out <FILEPATH>
          Optional relative filepath to the generated Plutus blueprint. Default to printing to
          stdout when omitted

  -m, --module <MODULE>
          Name of the validator's module within the project. Optional if there's only one validator

  -v, --validator <VALIDATOR>
          Name of the validator within the module. Optional if there's only one validator

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
